entries.title: Artemis: Efficient Commit-and-Prove SNARKs for zkML
entries.scope: Generic commit-and-prove SNARK construction linking a proof witness to externally committed values through homomorphic polynomial commitments, with a Halo2 zkML implementation.
limitations: The external commitment must support the construction's homomorphic polynomial-commitment interface; Pearl's keyed BLAKE3 matrix root is not such a commitment, so Artemis is not a drop-in Pearl bridge.
The evaluation and speedups are author-reported and were not reproduced by Aeye.
Witness-to-model commitment consistency does not by itself establish native work, activation origin, full execution, hardware provenance, or demand.

entries.title: DeepProve: Verifiable End-to-End Large Language Model Inference
entries.scope: End-to-end proof relation for quantized GPT-2 and Gemma 3 autoregressive inference.
limitations: Performance is author-reported and not reproduced by Aeye.
The relation is quantized arithmetic, not native GPU semantics, physical work, or demand.

entries.title: Proof of Demand Is Not Proof of Work: On the Limits of Demand-Weighted Consensus under Free Pseudonyms
entries.scope: Separates work soundness, job binding, and demand exogeneity and gives conditional impossibility and cost results for certifying economically independent demand from endogenous receipts under free pseudonyms.
limitations: The demand-indistinguishability theorem is conditional on its fungibility, coalition-control, realizability, or indistinguishability premises; exogenous trust roots or costly provenance may change the setting.
It supplies no construction for Pearl-specific execution binding and does not make every demand signal impossible.
The paper is a preprint and its deployed-system discussion was not independently reproduced by Aeye.

entries.title: DiFR: Inference Verification Despite Nondeterminism
entries.scope: Statistical token and activation divergence signals for inference auditing.
limitations: Detection depends on the reference, null distribution, attack distribution, and sample size.
It is not cryptographic execution soundness.

entries.title: Evidence-Bound Gateway-Path Provenance for Third-Party LLM Inference
entries.scope: TEE-backed request, policy, route, endpoint-observation, and encrypted-stream provenance for third-party LLM gateways.
limitations: The construction assumes an uncompromised TEE, attestation root, release-signing path, verifier, and dependency supply chain.
It explicitly does not prove that the upstream provider served the claimed model or executed inference correctly.
It does not bind Pearl commitments or establish useful work or independent demand; prototype results are author-reported and were not reproduced by Aeye.

entries.title: Hawkeye: Reproducing GPU-Level Non-Determinism
entries.scope: CPU reproduction of selected NVIDIA Tensor Core MMA arithmetic.
limitations: Instruction-level empirical conformance is not execution provenance or device identity.
It does not cover complete inference glue.

entries.title: Hollow-LLM Attack: Computationally Trivial Weights in Zero-Knowledge Verification of LLM Inference
entries.scope: Separation attack between a valid inference relation and substantial computational effort.
limitations: The concrete ghost-weight constructions do not establish that every proof system admits the same shortcut.
It directly motivates keeping WORK separate from EXECUTION.

entries.title: IMMACULATE: A Practical LLM Auditing Framework via Verifiable Computation
entries.scope: Selective auditing against a trusted CPU-TEE reference.
limitations: Low fleet overhead is obtained by auditing a small request fraction.
Assurance depends on prevalence assumptions and the TEE/reference path.

entries.title: Kernel Contracts: A Specification Language for ML Kernel Correctness Across Heterogeneous Silicon
entries.scope: Vocabulary and proposed specification language for ML kernel correctness claims.
limitations: It is a proposal, not an independent verifier or retained cross-device conformance result.

entries.title: Towards Verifiable AI with Lightweight Cryptographic Proofs of Inference
entries.scope: Post-commit random path checks with local transition recomputation.
limitations: Worst-case concentrated corruption can have weak detection under a single path.
Cleartext openings can expose model or trace data.

entries.title: Bit-Accurate Modeling of GPU Matrix Multiply-Accumulate Units: Demystifying Numerical Discrepancy and Accuracy
entries.scope: Bit-accurate empirical MMA models across selected NVIDIA and AMD architectures.
limitations: An arithmetic oracle does not establish physical origin or complete execution.

entries.title: NanoZK: Privacy-Preserving Verifiable Inference for Large Language Models via Layerwise Zero-Knowledge Proofs
entries.scope: Proposed layerwise Halo2/IPA proof chain for LLM inference.
limitations: GPT-2-scale values are projected rather than measured in the retained version.
Advertised code was not retained at the cited location and reported tables require independent reconciliation.

entries.title: Proofs of Useful Work from Arbitrary Matrix Multiplication
entries.scope: PoUW from arbitrary matrix multiplication with asymptotically vanishing honest overhead.
limitations: Security relies on the paper's non-standard batch low-rank correlated-equations conjecture.
Economic value is explicitly separated and omitted from the technical construction.
It does not bind a complete request/model/trace/output relation.

entries.title: The Usefulness Gap in Proof-of-Useful-Work: An Empirical Study of Pearl's cuPOW Protocol
entries.scope: Empirical demonstration that Pearl-accepted work can be generated from random matrices without inference.
limitations: The retained experiment establishes accepted random-matrix shares in the sampled setting, not the state of every network job.
Network-wide and energy estimates are author claims not reproduced by Aeye.

entries.title: Pearl Research Labs Whitepaper

entries.scope: Project whitepaper describing Pearl network design and economics.
limitations: The exact upstream URL, publication date, and immutable version identifier were not retained; the digest records a private review input that is not part of the public replay surface.
Whitepaper statements are project claims, not independent validation.

entries.title: Pearl Floating Point Scheme Specification
entries.scope: Proposed FP8 PoUW scheme with post-noise quantization, tile recomputation, jackpot policy, useful-miner path, and bit-exact verifier arithmetic.
limitations: The core quantized-subspace hardness premise is an explicit informal assumption, not a reduction to a standard assumption.
The document specifies a proposed floating-point work protocol, not request/model/output execution or external demand.
Its protocol and measured arithmetic claims require independent review against the exact open implementation and B200 vectors.

entries.title: TEE.fail: Breaking Trusted Execution Environments via DDR5 Memory Bus Interposition
entries.version: 47th IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy, 2026
entries.scope: Physical DDR5 interposition attacks against contemporary server TEEs and downstream GPU attestation trust.
limitations: Physical attacks may be outside some deployment threat models but must remain an explicit residual assumption.

entries.title: TensorCommitments: A Lightweight Verifiable Inference for Language Models
entries.scope: Tensor-native position-binding commitments and sampled openings.
limitations: The retained construction binds openings but does not independently establish every layer transition relation.
Reported detection is empirical rather than negligible cryptographic soundness.

entries.title: Verde: Verification via Refereed Delegation for Machine Learning Programs
entries.scope: Optimistic duplicate execution and bisection to a disputed operator.
limitations: Assurance requires at least one honest participant, data availability, and deterministic reference semantics.
Duplicate computation is total system cost even when provider overhead is reported separately.

entries.title: VeriLLM: A Lightweight Framework for Publicly Verifiable Decentralized Inference
entries.scope: One-honest-verifier decentralized inference checking with incentives.
limitations: Assurance is conditional on an honest verifier and the economic model.
The retained overhead components require independent reconciliation before repeating a single percentage headline.

entries.title: zkGPT: An Efficient Non-interactive Zero-knowledge Proof Framework for LLM Inference
entries.scope: Non-interactive zero-knowledge proof relation for quantized GPT-2 inference.
limitations: The encoded circuit is not native GPU arithmetic and does not establish external work or demand.
Performance is workload- and platform-specific.

entries.title: Maverick: Private and Verifiable LLM Inference Made Practical via Matrix-Vector Multiplication Delegation
entries.scope: Information-theoretically sound delegated matrix-vector multiplication with transparent preprocessing, batch verification, and optional input privacy; Qwen3-4B prototype.
limitations: The client still performs nonlinear operations in the described end-to-end architecture.
Matrix-vector delegation is not by itself a public transferable receipt, proof of work, full server event-DAG proof, or demand evidence.
All speed figures are author-reported.

entries.title: Sound Debloating of Redundant Checks in Zero-Knowledge Machine-Learning Circuits
entries.scope: Provenance-guided removal of redundant zkML constraints with a stated witness-set preservation argument.
limitations: Soundness is conditional on implemented transfer and entailment rules and the exact compiled circuit.
Constraint and prover-time reductions are author-reported and do not change the proved relation's semantic scope.

entries.title: Repeated-Game Security for Restaking-Based Verifiable Inference
entries.scope: Repeated-game analysis of restaking-based verifiable inference and a history-dependent challenge/reputation/vesting mechanism.
limitations: The security result is incentive compatibility for a stated repeated-game model, not cryptographic execution soundness.
Detection response, discount factors, stake ownership, collusion, and economic calibration remain explicit assumptions.
Performance and incentive improvements are author-reported and not reproduced by Aeye.

entries.title: zkComposer: Decomposing Proof Construction to Scale zkML
entries.scope: Parallel proof construction through contiguous-layer subproofs linked by shared activation commitments.
limitations: Linking preserves only the underlying relation and assumptions; it does not add WORK, native semantics, or demand.
Reported speedups are author claims against named baselines.

entries.title: Jolt Atlas: Verifiable Inference via Lookup Arguments in Zero Knowledge
entries.scope: Lookup-centric zkML over ONNX operations with streaming-prover and zero-knowledge techniques.
limitations: ONNX/circuit semantics are not native serving-engine or GPU semantics.
The retained paper does not compose external work or demand evidence.

entries.title: JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS)
entries.scope: Deterministic JSON representation for hashing and signing.
limitations: The executable research profile uses a deliberately narrower JSON value domain and is not yet a production wire profile.

entries.title: Concise Binary Object Representation (CBOR)
entries.scope: CBOR data model, encoding, and deterministic-encoding guidance.
limitations: Aeye has not accepted a CBOR/CDDL wire profile or assigned private labels.

entries.title: CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE): Structures and Process
entries.scope: Standard protection structures for signed or encrypted CBOR objects.
limitations: A valid COSE signature authenticates a statement; it does not establish that the statement is true.

entries.title: Remote ATtestation procedureS (RATS) Architecture
entries.scope: Roles and conceptual messages for evidence, appraisal, attestation results, and relying-party policy.
limitations: It is an architecture and vocabulary, not an Aeye execution relation or proof backend.

entries.title: The Entity Attestation Token (EAT)
entries.scope: Authenticated claim sets for entity attestation using CWT or JWT profiles.
limitations: EAT is appropriate for attestation evidence and results under a profile, not a generic substitute for Pearl or ZK proof semantics.

entries.title: An Architecture for Trustworthy and Transparent Digital Supply Chains
entries.scope: SCITT architecture for signed statements, transparency services, receipts, and relying-party policy.
limitations: Transparency provides history and accountability but does not prevent a dishonest issuer or make a registered statement true.

entries.title: Remote ATtestation procedureS (RATS) Conceptual Message Wrapper (CMW)
entries.scope: Standard wrapper and indicators for RATS evidence, endorsements, reference values, appraisal policies, and attestation results.
limitations: CMW identifies and transports conceptual messages; it does not define the Aeye claim relations or upgrade evidence.
